senses.gloss: m. ch. (רְבַב) gradation, conclusion a minori ad majus (= קַל וָחוֹמֶר).
units: Y. Peah IV, 18ᵇ top ר׳ דר׳ יוחנן ור׳ דר״ל there exists one argument a minori by R. J. and another by R. S. ben L.; ר׳ … מה מציאה וכ׳ R. J.’s argument is: if in the case of a find &c. (v. corr. vers in Frankel, Talm. Hierosol.).—ר׳, דר׳ (cmp. חוֹמֶר I) something greater, more restrictive.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 17:1:2">Y. Sabb. XVII, beg. 16ᵃ</cite> <he>דלתות הבית דר׳ ודלתות הכלים דר׳ וכ׳</he> (not <he>דרובן</he>) in one respect there is a greater restriction in the law concerning the moving of the doors of a house, and in another respect a greater restriction in the law concerning the doors of furniture; <he>דלתות … דר׳ וכ׳</he> the greater restriction concerning the doors of a house consists in this that they dare not be moved even &c.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 1:6:5">Y. Ab. Zar. I, 40ᵃ</cite> top <he>ר׳ דר״ש ב״ל מדרבי וכ׳</he> the opinion of R. S. b. L. goes farther in restriction than that of R. J.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Maasrot 1:4:4">Y. Maasr. I, 49ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>דר׳ אתא אימור לך</he> he comes to tell you something greater.—

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 1:9:5">Y. Meg. I, 71ᶜ</cite> top <he>דרַבָּה שהספרים וכ׳</he> here is something greater (than the difference between scrolls and T’fillin which has been stated): scrolls may be written on either side of the parchment &c.; <he>דף אחד בשני עורות לית היא דר׳</he> the ‘one column’ law against the ‘two sides’ law—this is no gradation.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Peah 1:1:31">Y. Peah I, 15ᵈ</cite> top <he>והוא דרבה מִנָּהּ גדול … כפריעת חוב וכ׳</he> (not <he>בפריעת</he>) here is something greater (just the reverse, v. <cite ref="A00449"><he>אַדְּרַבָּא</he></cite>); greater is a duty which is like paying a debt (the filial duty) than &c.; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 1:7:14">Y. Kidd. I, 61ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>וההיא דרבנין</he> (corr. acc.).
